chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, then it became clear to him after he had consummated the marriage with her that she had a absent husband, so he left her. Then the husband arrived and divorced her or died, leaving her. Should he marry her again, this same man who married her and did not know she had a husband? He said: 'I do not like for him to marry her until she marries another husband.'

key_terms.تَنْكِحَ زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُ: She marries another husband (a different man)
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman if her absent husband returns after she has already married another man?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *Istibra* for a woman in a state of *Gharar* (uncertainty) regarding her marital status, specifically when her absent husband's fate is unknown. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises against the second husband remarrying her directly after the first husband's departure or death, preferring she undergo a full cycle of marriage to a third party to ensure absolute clarity and remove any residual doubt about her lineage or status. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on caution (*Ihtiyat*) in matters of lineage (*Nasab*) and marital validity.
